title: Requesting D-Clearance at USC Dornsife (Spring 2027 undergraduate courses)
text:
Note: this page covers undergraduate courses for Spring 2027. It does not define D-clearance. It lists which office handles requests by course prefix, and gives department examples. The full course-by-course list is on the original page.

BEFORE REQUESTING
- The page recommends that you "meet with your academic advisor" to confirm the course fits your academic plan and progress. Advising resources: dornsife.usc.edu/advising/.

WHICH OFFICE HANDLES REQUESTS
- General Education (GE) office: courses with prefixes GESM, FESM, MDA and INDS. See dornsife.usc.edu/ge/registration/.
- Thematic Option (TO) advisor: CORE-prefix thematic option courses.
- Graduate students: contact your Master's or PhD program advisor directly.
- All other courses: the department or instructor listed for each course, usually through a form or email.

EXAMPLES BY DEPARTMENT
- Humanities: many English, American Studies and Gender and Sexuality Studies courses use a Qualtrics form. Art History and Directed Research courses go through Professor Samantha Burton (burtons@usc.edu). Spanish and French language courses use a form on the languages D-clearance page; some need instructor approval if added after Week 1.
- Social Sciences: Anthropology uses a D-Clearance form. Economics courses go through econ@usc.edu. Sociology Directed Research requires an advisor-issued form, instructor signature, and emailing soci@usc.edu.
- Life Sciences: several courses require approval from a named lab manager, program specialist or instructor. Human Biology uses a D-clearance form.
- Physical Sciences and Math: Earth Sciences, Mathematics, and Physics and Astronomy each have their own form. Chemistry lab sections use a waitlist form; lecture sections go to coord105@usc.edu.

RESTRICTIONS AND DEADLINES NOTED ON THE PAGE
- IR-397 (Field Research in Human Rights): application only, deadline November 2, 2026.
- Some courses are application only or limited to specific students, such as HIST-212 (Spring Semester in D.C. students only) and WRIT-340 sections (Business/Cinematic Arts students only, or DC campus only).
- Some courses are full with waitlists closed, including BISC-300, BISC-364, BISC-423 and BISC-431.
- Some Maymester courses are abroad and go through the Dornsife Faculty Led Programs (FLP) website.
- ENST-298A/B (Scientific Diving) requires a Maymester application, then open water dive certification, an AAUS medical authorization, diving accident insurance and a swim test.
- Psychology seat releases follow a published schedule; PSYC-100 equivalents need waivers in some cases.
